review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines two predicates, `IsProjectiveMeasureFamily` and `IsProjectiveLimit`, plus lemmas about them. I searched Mathlib for competing projective-family or projective-limit notions. In MeasureTheory, `IsProjectiveMeasureFamily` is declared only in this file. `ProjectiveFamilyContent.lean` builds a content from it, and the Probability files (`ProductMeasure`, `FiniteDimensionalLaws`, `IonescuTulcea/Traj`, `BrownianMotion/GaussianProjectiveFamily`) all reuse these two predicates. I found no parallel definition elsewhere in Mathlib. Both predicates are just `Measure.map` equalities along `Finset.restrict₂` and `Finset.restrict`. They are named specialisations used widely, so they are not avoidable duplicates. The other matches for "projective" were unrelated: projective modules, objects and varieties. I found nothing to report under this rubric.
